story: The first word everyone learns — literally “you good”.
言 (speech) beside 射 — thanks delivered in words. The second syllable goes neutral: xièxie, not xièxiè.
Literally “on horseback” — in ancient China nothing moved faster than a mounted messenger.
Fire + vehicle + station: a “fire-cart stop”. Early steam trains really were fire carts.
Word for word: “very long no see” — the English phrase is widely said to be a calque of this.
“Pearl milk tea” — invented in Taiwan; the tapioca balls are the 珍珠, pearls.
Literally “add oil” — refuel! Shouted at races, exams, and friends having a hard week.
Night + market. Where Taiwan actually eats dinner.
